package_info.package_name: Multiple (see list in report, e.g., @anemone95/evil, ca-certificates, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are flagged as dependency confusion candidates, often published as proof-of-concept (PoC) exercises. They are considered malicious because they exploit the dependency confusion attack vector, where attackers publish packages with names matching internal dependencies to public registries, potentially leading to unintentional installation and code execution in victim environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or install-time (depending on package type and configuration)
execution_context.file_location: package entry point (e.g., index.js for npm, __init__.py/setup.py for PyPI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or install-time, the code executes a benign or proof-of-concept action (such as logging a message or exfiltrating environment variables), demonstrating the ability to execute arbitrary code if the package is installed due to dependency confusion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Any code that executes automatically upon installation or import, especially in packages with names matching internal dependencies, is highly suspicious as it demonstrates the potential for supply chain compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute arbitrary code on install/import, especially without user intent. These packages are designed to prove that code execution is possible if dependency confusion occurs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may log messages or perform setup actions at install/import, but not with the intent to demonstrate or exploit dependency confusion.
key_indicators: Package name matches known internal/private dependencies
No legitimate functionality beyond PoC or demonstration
May include exfiltration or logging of environment variables

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a package to a public registry (npm/PyPI) with a name matching an internal/private dependency used by a target organization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's build or CI/CD system installs the malicious package instead of the intended internal one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the package executes at install-time or import-time, potentially exfiltrating data or demonstrating code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Proof-of-concept demonstration or actual compromise of the build environment.

behavioral_signatures: Package names matching internal/private dependencies appearing on public registries
Unexpected logging or exfiltration of environment variables
file_indicators: index.js or __init__.py/setup.py with code that executes on import/install
Packages with minimal or no legitimate functionality
network_indicators: Outbound network requests during install/import (if exfiltration is attempted)
Connections to attacker-controlled domains (in non-benign PoCs)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of packages from public registries whose names match internal/private dependencies. Flag packages that execute code on install/import, especially if they perform network operations or access sensitive environment variables. Use allow-lists for approved package sources and names, and block or quarantine suspicious packages pending review.
